newsitem.title: USA: CBOE says SEC okays new position limit, hedge rule.
newsitem.headline: CBOE says SEC okays new position limit, hedge rule.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange said the Securities and Exchange Commission has approved revised rules governing position limits and the hedge exemption in some broad-based CBOE index products.

The CBOE, in a statement late on Thursday, said the SEC approved an increase in the standard position and exercise limits in Standard & Poor's 500 (SPX) index options to 100,000 contracts from 45,000 on the same side of the market.
The maximum hedge exemption in SPX increased to 250,000 contracts from 135,000 for a single account, which will help accommodate institutional hedgers, CBOE said.
The SEC also extended for the first time the hedge exemption to broker-dealers, a CBOE spokesman said.

The SEC allowed an expanded range of products that hedgers may use in portfolios to qualify for the exemption to any product based on an underlying index that is margined by the Options Clearing Corp as part of the SPX product group.
In addition, the SEC approved using broad-based listed index options, warrants, futures and futures-options as well as stock baskets to qualify for index hedge exemptions.
The revised rules took effect on September 16, CBOE's spokesman added. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
